title: AI‑Agentic Cloud Era: Serverless GPU, Azure Cobalt, and Rising Security Stakes (Nov 2026)
core_insight: AI‑agentic, high‑performance compute is becoming the core differentiator across AWS, Google Cloud and Azure, while emerging security and regulatory pressures add new risk dimensions.

dimension_texts.technology: AWS Lambda now supports GPU instances enabling serverless high‑performance workloads; Google Cloud launches AI‑agent‑driven Managed Airflow and sidecar‑less Ambient Networking for GKE; Azure introduces Azure Catalyst and Cobalt 200 VM built for the agentic AI era, expanding native AI integration across the three major clouds. AWS adds S3 Tables managed migration to Apache Iceberg and Continuum for code‑vulnerability detection; Azure rolls out AI‑focused infrastructure innovations and AI‑centric billing models via Catalyst; Cloudflare integrates AI models (Clairic) into Workers and opens Kitesurf browser engine; Volcengine releases full‑stack cloud products including ByteHouse and DataLeap, strengthening data‑layer capabilities. AWS Lambda now supports GPU instances for Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances Amazon S3 Tables now offer managed migration of Apache Hive tables to Apache Iceberg AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available Drowning in clicks: Scaling Black Friday pipelines with Managed Airflow agents Introducing ambient networking for GKE How to simplify cloud access with Unified Access Policies, now in preview Introducing Azure Catalyst agentic modernization and new AI infrastructure innovations Azure Cobalt 200 VMs now available, proven on real workloads and built for the agentic era Continuous improvement comes to Microsoft Foundry
dimension_texts.infrastructure: AWS Lambda GPU adds a new high‑compute pricing tier; Azure Catalyst hints at finer‑grained AI compute billing; Cloudflare Spend Management introduces consumption caps for Workers and Durable Objects, suggesting future regional or tiered pricing adjustments. GPU instances on Lambda raise serverless compute ceiling; Azure Cobalt 200 VM uses custom silicon for dense AI workloads; Volcengine expands compute supply in China with its full‑stack cloud product suite; AWS continues to harden isolation with Nitro Sandboxes.
